summary: Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from circa 1977 to 1981 and later served as a professor there around 2000.
Seikō Hirata was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu and Bokuo Seki. He held a post at Hanazono University from circa 1965 to 1994.
Sein Tin was a scholar in linguistics and other fields who studied at Basic Education High School No. 9 Mawlamyine, the University of Rangoon, Christ Church, and under Pe Maung Tin from 1924 to 1927.
Seiran Ouchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a lecturer (jiko) at Nishi Hongan-ji and as president of Toyo University from 1914 to 1918.

Seiren Matsunami was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and under Walther Schubring. He served as a professor at Kyushu University (circa 1950–1967) and Rissho University (circa 1971–1979).

Seishi Karashima was a Buddhist studies, sinology, and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Cambridge, and Peking University under mentors including Minoru Hara, Xianlin Ji, and Oskar von Hinüber, later becoming a professor at Soka University.

Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar educated at Toyo University and Shingiyaha Daigakurin. He served as president of Buzan University, Taisho University, and Toyo University, while also teaching at the University of Tokyo and Rissho University.
Seitatsu Matsunami was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and was attested as a professor at Taisho University in 1992.

Seizan Yanagida was a Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology scholar. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, and held posts at Hanazono University, Kyoto University, and Chubu University.
Sen Wang was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University from circa 1931 to 1935 and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1952 to 1991.

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who, in 1999, held posts as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University from circa 1936 to 1937.
Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University and the University of Washington, later serving as a professor at Rissho University in 1972.

Sengaku Mayeda was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo, UPenn, and Münster under Hajime Nakamura and W. Norman Brown. He held professorships at Tokyo, Gakushuin, and Musashino, and chaired the Society for the Promotion of Buddhism.

Senkyo Sakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University, where he later served as a professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985), as well as a staff member at the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra.

Senmyo Naniwa is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University and studied under P. V. Bapat and Genjun Sasaki. In 2005, he held posts at Bukkyo University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
Sensho Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University from circa 1962 to 1971 and later served there as a professor from circa 1983 to 2008.

Sensho Murakami was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani and Toyo universities. He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo and as principal of Etchu Kyoko and Tokyo High School.

Seraphim Rose was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at San Diego High School, USC, California Institute of Integral Studies under Alan Watts, and UC Berkeley. He later served in the Russian Orthodox Patriarchal Parishes in the USA.

Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev at Saint Petersburg State University. He became a professor there, led the Imperial Academy of Sciences, and directed the Asiatic Museum.
